problem_statement: The sys_heap allocator lacks per-chunk canary-based corruption detection. When CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_FULL is set, the heap should store a canary value at the end of each allocated chunk (computed from the chunk address and size, XORed with a magic constant), validate it on free/realloc/size queries, and poison it after freeing to detect double-free. Buffer overflows that corrupt the trailer must be caught at free time. The heap sizing constants (Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE, Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE_FOR) must also account for the additional trailer overhead so that a heap initialized to the minimum size can still satisfy a 1-byte allocation.

verification.reason: The problem statement describes the heap canary feature well but omits the CMake build-time constants function that a major hidden test exercises, the CHUNK_TRAILER_SIZE macro name, and the full set of hardening Kconfig options. All gaps can be repaired by specifying the public interface without dictating implementation details.

problems.detail: The hidden tests include a full standalone test for a new CMake function zephyr_constants_library() (tests/cmake/constants_library/) that the problem statement does not describe at all. The statement only says heap sizing constants must 'account for trailer overhead' but does not mention that they must be computed at build time via this CMake function, nor the function's name, parameters (NAME, SOURCE, HEADER, INCLUDES, DEPENDS), or its behavior (compile a C file with GEN_ABSOLUTE_SYM, generate a header under include/generated/zephyr/).
The heap_align test uses CHUNK_TRAILER_SIZE * CHUNK_UNIT in its suffix calculation, but the problem statement never names this macro.

The testcase.yaml files reference CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_NONE, but the problem statement only mentions CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_FULL. The full set of hardening levels (NONE, BASIC, MODERATE, FULL, EXTREME) and the CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_CANARIES bool option are not mentioned.

leak_check.leak_detail: Minor leaks: the phrase 'Existing code and tests rely' mentions tests, and the canary XOR computation / include-guard derivation are more implementation detail than needed. The rest describes public interface, macros, Kconfig options, and build-module behaviour that the hidden tests use.
leak_check.suggested_statement:
The sys_heap allocator lacks per-chunk canary-based corruption detection. When CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_FULL is set, the heap should store a canary value at the end of each allocated chunk, validate it on free/realloc/size queries, and poison it after freeing to detect double-free. Buffer overflows that corrupt the trailer must be caught at free time. The heap sizing constants (Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE, Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE_FOR) must also account for the additional trailer overhead so that a heap initialized to the minimum size can still satisfy a 1-byte allocation.

The trailer size must be exposed as the macro CHUNK_TRAILER_SIZE (measured in chunk units); it is non-zero when canary-based hardening is enabled and zero otherwise. Existing code relies on this macro to compute suffix sizes and full-heap allocation sizes.

A Kconfig choice SYS_HEAP_HARDENING must be added with at least two options: CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_NONE (disables all heap validation checks) and CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_FULL (enables per-chunk canary validation). Other intermediate levels (BASIC, MODERATE, EXTREME) may also be defined.

Additionally, a CMake function zephyr_constants_library() must be implemented. It accepts parameters NAME, SOURCE, an optional HEADER (defaulting to <name>.h), an optional INCLUDES list, and an optional DEPENDS list. It creates an OBJECT library from a C source file containing GEN_ABSOLUTE_SYM declarations, then generates a header under include/generated/zephyr/ containing the resulting symbols (those ending in _OFFSET or _SIZEOF). The DEPENDS parameter ensures that another constants library's generated header is produced before this library is compiled. Generated headers must have include guards that avoid collisions between multiple generated headers.
